chunks: And with this chain, from Al-Ridha (peace be upon him), from his father Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: A man came to As-Sadiq (peace be upon him) and said,

‘I am fed up with the world, so I ask God for death.’ He said, ‘Ask for life so that you may obey [God], not so that you may disobey. That you live and obey is better for you than that you die having neither obeyed nor disobeyed.’
ai.seo_question: What did the Imam advise a man to ask for when he was tired of the world and desired death?
ai.summary: This tradition from *Uyun Akhbar al-Rida* highlights the Shia emphasis on the continuity of worship (*ibadah*) through life, countering the notion of *khuruj min al-dunya* (exiting the world) via premature death. Imam al-Rida (s) advises seeking life not for worldly indulgence, but to maximize the opportunity for obedience, framing existence as a necessary vessel for spiritual attainment.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 30-3 According to the same documentation, it has been narrated on the authority of Al-Ridha (s) on the authority of his father Musa ibn Ja’far (s), “A man went to see As-Sadiq (s) and said,

‘I am fed up with this world and ask God for my death.’ The Imam (s) told him, ‘It is better that you ask God to live so that you can obey Him. It is better for you to live and obey God, than to die and have neither disobeyed or obeyed God.’”
